more.def: A bright blue-green color, between blue and green.

easy.def: A harmful attempt to break into computers.
examples: A cyberattack can shut a website down.

more.def: An attempt to break into a computer system to damage it or steal information.
examples: A cyberattack shut down the website for a day.
The bank stopped the cyberattack before any money was lost.
Experts work hard to protect computers from a cyberattack.

easy.def: A person who is mean to others online.
examples: Tell a grown-up about a cyberbully.

more.def: A person who uses phones or computers to be cruel to other people.
examples: A cyberbully sends mean messages online.
Tell a grown-up if you ever meet a cyberbully.
The cyberbully hurt her classmate's feelings.

easy.def: To be mean to someone online.
examples: She would not cyberbully her friend.

more.def: To use phones or computers to be cruel to someone.
examples: She was cyberbullied by a stranger online and told her parents.
The school teaches kids not to cyberbully others.

easy.def: Being mean to someone again and again online.
examples: Cyberbullying can make someone feel sad.

more.def: Using phones or computers to be cruel to someone again and again, such as by sending mean messages.
examples: Cyberbullying is unkind, and it can make a person feel very sad.
If you see cyberbullying, tell a grown-up you trust.
Our school has rules against cyberbullying.

easy.def: Keeping computers and their information safe.

more.def: The ways people protect computers and the information on them from harm or theft.
examples: Strong passwords are part of good cybersecurity.
Banks spend a lot of money on cybersecurity to protect customers' information.
Our school teaches cybersecurity so students can stay safe online.

more.def: The imaginary space where computers and the internet connect people.
examples: Cyberspace connects computers around the world.

easy.def: A being that is part human and part machine.
examples: The cyborg is in the story.

more.def: A being, in stories, that is partly human and partly machine.
examples: In the movie, the cyborg had a metal arm.
A cyborg is part person and part robot.
The cyborg helped save the city.

easy.def: A set of events that repeat.

more.def: A series of events that happen again and again in the same order.
examples: The water cycle moves water from the sea to the sky and back.
The seasons form a cycle each year.
The washing machine finished its cycle.
I cycle to school every day.
She cycled to the library on her new bike.

easy.def: Happening again and again in the same order.

more.def: Happening in a cycle, so that the same events repeat over and over in the same order.
examples: The seasons are cyclical, so spring always follows winter.
The water cycle is cyclical, with rain falling and rising again.
A farm's work is cyclical, with planting and harvesting each year.

easy.def: A person who rides a bike.

more.def: A person who rides a bicycle.
examples: The cyclist wore a helmet and rode along the bike path.
A cyclist raced up the hill.
The cyclists rode in a long line.

easy.def: A strong wind that spins in a circle.

more.def: A large storm with strong winds that spin around a center.
examples: A cyclone hit the island with heavy rain.
The cyclone tore branches from the trees.
The village prepared for the cyclone.
A gray cygnet followed its mother across the pond.
A cygnet grows into a white swan.

easy.def: A shape like a can, with flat round ends.

more.def: A shape with straight sides and two flat, round ends of the same size, like a can or a tube.
examples: A soup can is shaped like a cylinder.
The teacher held up a cylinder and asked us to count its flat faces.
Each of the tall candles was a perfect cylinder.

easy.def: Shaped like a tube or can.

more.def: Shaped like a cylinder, with round, flat ends and straight sides.
examples: A cylindrical tower stood by the castle.
The pipe was long and cylindrical.

easy.def: Two round metal plates that you crash together.

more.def: Two round metal plates that are struck together to make a ringing sound.
examples: The cymbals made a loud ringing sound.
She played the cymbals in the band.

easy.def: A tall, dark tree that stays green.

more.def: A tall evergreen tree with dark green leaves, often found in warm places.
examples: Tall cypresses lined the road to the villa.
The cypress grows in swamps and warm hills.
A cypress tree stood in the old garden.
